title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
content:
## Present Perfect vs Past Simple

Compare unspecified time and life experience with finished actions at a specific past time.

### Lesson focus

1. Present perfect: I have lost my wallet.
2. Past simple: I lost my wallet yesterday.
3. Present perfect: She has made a cake.
4. Past simple: She made a cake for his birthday.
5. Present perfect: They have visited Paris.
6. Past simple: They visited Paris last summer.

### Understand the pattern

Present perfect links an earlier event to the present without naming a finished past time. Past simple describes an event in a completed past period. Compare a present result, an experience and a dated event before choosing the tense.

### Worked answers and explanation

'I have lost my wallet' emphasises the current problem. 'I lost my wallet yesterday' places the loss in a finished past time. 'They have visited Paris' reports experience, while 'They visited Paris last summer' names a completed period. Have been to commonly describes a visit followed by a return; have gone to normally implies the person has not yet returned.

### Try another

Complete: She ___ three books so far this month. (read)

### Suggested answer

Has read. So far and the still-current month connect the completed reading with now. Read is the past participle here, although its spelling matches the base form.
